main_text.p: bus & humectantibus partim cerebro rafo, partim pedum soleis : aut etiam ipsis testi-bus admotis, aut mammis uti necesse est. Si praeterea stomachica syncope ęgrum infester cum nausea, tunc vomitum procurabimus, sicut iam ostendimus. Si vero ea sit cardiaca, licet lethum nobis significer, attamen vini boni & odorati potu, & facie aceto afperfa, ęgrum reuocabimus, cardiacaq; cū iusculis pulli propinantes. Ad hoc summum symptoma maxime conferre dicitur antidotus e cocco baphico, seu grano infestorio, quod Kermes est Arabū. Quod si desideretur, eius loco electarium e gemmis, quod eximie roborat cor, tum exhibebimus: dein incendium, quod invehere potuit suis aromatib. calidioribus, succo oxalidis, aut citrij, aut limonij, vel arancij temperabimus. Ratio victus in huiusmodi affectibus minime contemnenda est, quoniam non parui est momenti. Lōge enim alia esse debet, quàm in aliis acutis, in quibus victus plenior esse debet in principio, quàm in incremento, & in hoc quàin statu: quando videlicet tenuissimo victu, hoc est (quē-admodum explicat Galenus ) fola ptisana est utendum. page.notes: Transcribed as printed; the scan is faint in places. "quàin" in "hoc quàin statu" is doubtful and may be a printing error for "quàm in statu"; the word is marked [?] in the text below in the sense of a reading uncertainty. Running head shows "CAVSAS" with V as a consonant in capitals; given as CAUSAS per the vowel rule. Forms like "uiftus" and "fyncope" are read as "victus" and "syncope" from their long-s and ligature spelling. The small dot in the right margin is ink or stain, not text, and is left out. The reference mark "ę" after "syncope" and "afperfa" is the printed ę ligature, kept as printed. The catchword "crates" and the signature "I 5" are in the bottom margin.
